p: Sheffield has a knack for reinventing itself. The city that made its name on steel and cutlery now has a city centre full of new squares, independent food spots and nightlife, and Charter Square sits right in the middle of that change. It's a handy, central spot where student crowds, work groups and families of grown-ups all end up rubbing shoulders.

Getting here is straightforward. Sheffield station is a manageable walk away, up through Sheaf Square and the city centre, and the Supertram stops around the centre will get you close if you're coming in from further out. Bus links along this side of town are good too, which helps if the evening runs later than planned.

If you're new to bowling, don't worry. The main trick is to slow down, aim at the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, and let the ball do the work. The rest is luck and a bit of swagger. For groups, it's worth giving every team a mix of ages and abilities, so nobody ends up stuck on the losing side all night. Mid-game snacks are encouraged.

Want to add a bit of culture? The Millennium Gallery in the centre covers everything from art to Sheffield's metalwork heritage. Football fans can look up the two big clubs, United at Bramall Lane and Wednesday at Hillsborough, for a bit of local rivalry to match the one you're about to start on the lanes. It all makes for a cracking day in South Yorkshire.
